topics.label: Introduction to the Hallmarks of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning objectives, context, and overall framework of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Sustaining Proliferative Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the receptor signaling cascades and genetic mutations that allow cancer cells to achieve autonomous growth and evade inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Differentiation Blocks in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how blocks in normal terminal differentiation promote malignancy across both hematopoietic and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the molecular mechanisms and regulatory factors that enable cancer cells to avoid programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells achieve unlimited replicative potential by overcoming telomere shortening and bypassing normal stress-induced senescence.

topics.label: Reprogramming of Cancer Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the Warburg effect, metabolic rewiring, and the role of oncometabolites in altering tumor epigenetics.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the necessity, progression, and molecular balance governing new blood vessel recruitment in developing tumors.

topics.label: Invasion and Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the multistep cascade of cancer cell dissemination, diagnostic tracking methods, and metastatic inefficiency.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer synthesizes the commonalities among cancer hallmarks and concludes the lecture.
